newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 21.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
FIVE-MEMBER CABINET FOR UTTAR PRADESH

A five-member Bahujan Samaj Party - Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) coalition ministry, headed by Mayawati, will assume office, ending president's rule in Uttar Pradesh. BJP leader and former prime minister A.B. Vajpayee said both the parties would have two cabinet ministers each. The second phase of ministry expansion would be decided shortly by senior leaders of the two parties. The new cabinet, after assuming office, would decide the date for convening the state legislature.
Indian Express
MAYAWATI GETS HER KEY MEN IN PLACE

Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) leader Mayawati begun asserting herself by appointing officials of her choice to key posts, even before taking over as chief minister of Uttar Pradesh. The decision to reshuffle officials was taken at a joint meeting with their coalition partner Bharatiya Janata Party.
The Times Of India
APEX COURT FOR PROBE PANEL TO BUST CRIMINAL SYNDICATES

The Supreme Court ordered the setting up of an independent body, enjoying the people's trust, to investigate into widespread development of crime syndicates. The syndicates, it said, had grown in the wake of a nexus between politicians, bureaucrats, media personalities and members of the judiciary in the country. Rejecting the government's plea for a nodal agency, the court said the agency, in its present form, may not command the people's confidence. The verdict was a fallout of petitions by some public interest bodies who sought disclosure of the names identified by the then home secretary in his report on the nexus.
VISA RESTRICTIONS FOR PAKISTANI NATIONALS EASED

As a unilateral gesture of goodwill aimed at promoting people-to-people contact, India announced a series of measures easing visa restrictions for Pakistani nationals. For the first time, Pakistani businessmen would be eligible for a one-year multi-entry visa. If they happen to travel by air, they would be able to exit and enter either through Bombay or Delhi.
The Economic Times
RECAST OF PUBLIC OFFER STIPULATION LIKELY

The Securities and Exchange Board of India plans to change the stipulation of 40 percent net offer to public in a public issue to give more flexibility to the issuers. This was part of wide-ranging reforms which the SEBI board would be considering in its next meeting. Apart from this, the validity of the acknowledgement card for public issues was also being extended to allow companies more freedom to choose their timing for entering the market. The reduction in lock-in period for promoters' contribution and preferential allotment from five to three years, the funding undersubscribed portion by promoters and the pricing of employee stock option schemes were also on the agenda of the March 26 meeting.
1.5 MLN TONNES OF WHEAT IMPORTS ON CARDS

The government plans fresh imports of 1.5 million tonnes of wheat, which would take total wheat imports to three million tonnes this year. As a preliminary move, the State Trading Corporation (STC) floated a global tender for 50,000 tonnes of wheat to test international prices. STC stipulated that the wheat contracted through this tender should reach India between July and September. Around 1.4 million tonnes of wheat have already been contracted to arrive over the next two months. Sources said the new tender gave STC the option to contract more than 50,000 tonnes if the price was favourable.
COURT RULING ON SCAM-TAINTED SHARES WINDFALL FOR BANKS

A Supreme Court ruling made commercial banks owners of shares worth billions bought from brokers involved in the securities scam. The Supreme Court changed a verdict of the special court looking into the share scam cases, regarding ready-forward deals entered into by banks with several stock brokers. The court said the banks had become the owners of the securities the moment they paid for the same. The agreement to sell in the future may be illegal but did not have a bearing on the ownership of the securities held by the banks, the court ruled.
RELIANCE TO RAISE $500 MLN FOR TELECOM

Reliance Industries (RIL) will shortly put in an application to the Finance Ministry for another external commercial borrowing to fund its basic telecommunication project. RIL has already raised close to $1 billion for various projects in the last 18 months and is likely to seek another $450-500 million for its telecom project. The company may even stagger its borrowing in two tranches. A telecom project could now borrow up to 50 percent of its project cost from abroad.
Financial Express
NEW SCHEME TO BOOST PUBLIC SECTOR INVESTMENT IN POWER

The finance minister promised a new programme to infuse public investment in the power sector. He also indicated likely changes in the customs and excise proposals made in the budget. Refuting criticism on the voluntary disclosure scheme, he said the new proposal envisaged taxing unaccounted money at 30 percent as against zero tax, as advocated by some.
GOVERNMENT FIRMS TO MOP UP 3,080 BLN RUPEES IN NINTH PLAN

Union government companies (CPSUs) are expected to mop up 3,080.11 billion rupees at 1996/97 prices, as internal and extra budgetary resources in the Ninth Plan period (1997/2002). This would be an increase of 40.3 percent in real terms over the Eighth Plan projections. Petroleum and natural gas, railways and the telecommunications sectors would have to mop up 1,601.58 billion rupees, representing 52 percent of the total amount to be raised by the CPSUs in the Ninth Plan. Power, steel, coal and surface transport taken together would be expected to mobilise 1,017.73 billion rupees as internal and extra-budgetary resources. Internal resources mobilisation for the power sector was pegged at 82.41 billion rupees.
FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS GO SLOW ON TELECOM FUNDING

Three financial institutions have decided to go slow on financing basic telecom projects. This was despite a recent agreement which stipulated Department of Telecommunication should compensate all lenders in basic telecom projects in case the operator's licence was terminated. The lukewarm response of the institutions will pave the way for foreign banks to take the lead in financing such projects. With financial institutions apprehensive of the risk exposure equation in these projects, the decision to go slow had nothing to do with the technical aspect of financing, sources said.
COMPULSORY REINSURANCE OF PRIVATE FIRMS' PORTFOLIOS MOOTED

Faced with the threat of international competition in health insurance, the General Insurance Corporation (GIC) advised the Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) to formulate guidelines restricting private foray into health insurance companies. GIC suggested that the minimum capital for health insurance companies be one billion rupees. In addition, GIC wanted private companies to reinsure their portfolio. GIC's worry on the health insurance front stemmed from the failure of its own health scheme. Almost 10 years after its launch, the four GIC subsidiaries were able to write only about 1.6 million policies.
MULTINATIONALS TURN TO GOVERNMENT BANKS FOR FUNDS

Multinational corporations (MNCs) are shifting the focus to state-owned (PSU) banks to access cheaper funds. Sources said at least four multinationals have left the fold of foreign banks and tied up with PSU banks in the last quarter of the current fiscal. A host of them were believed to be in the process of severing ties with their traditional bankers and establishing a new relationship with PSU banks as the cost of borrowing from state-run banks worked out to be at least 200 basis points cheaper than that of foreign banks.
Business Standard
ITOCHU PLANS ARM TO ROUTE INVESTMENTS

Itochu Corporation, the multi-billion dollar Japanese trading house, plans to set up a wholly owned subsidiary in India. All future investments in the country would be routed through this subsidiary. The company is working on investment and expansion strategies for the country and is expected to seek the government's approval.
GOLD, DIAMOND IMPORT RULES TO BE EASED

Imports of gold, diamond and rough stones will be made easier in the export-import policy for 1997/2002, to be announced on March 31, sources said. The Commerce Ministry is pressing to allow the import of certain inputs and consumables used by exporters of gems and jewellery at 25 percent duty. Besides, it is looking at the possibility of allowing duty-free import of rough coloured stones for export. The new policy may also allow more agencies, including foreign banks, to import gold under duty-exemption schemes.
COMPOSITE INFOTECH MINISTRY PLANNED

The government is considering a proposal to form a composite information technology ministry, by merging the ministries of communications, information and broadcasting and the department of electronics. The Finance Ministry evinced interest in the proposal put forward by leading trade associations. The chambers suggested making the Telecom Regulatory Authority (TRAI) the main regulatory body for the sector under the proposed ministry. The proposal formed part of the information technology industry's efforts to bring it on a par with the infrastructure sector. Financial institutions have also urged for relaxing the guidelines for funding information technology projects, giving a boost to the industry bodies' proposal.
FINANCE MINISTER AIMS TO FOCUS ON STATE FUNDING OF POWER

The government will soon devise an investment plan for the power sector which will have special emphasis on public investment. The finance minister discussed in parliament how the country failed to add the targeted 30,000 megawatts of additional generation during the eighth plan. He quoted Lenin to stress the need to leave all ideologies behind to attract investment in power generation and transmission. The Cogentrix power project in Karnataka was delayed as the power transmission bill had to be referred to the standing committee at the insistence of left parties.
THIRD NATIONAL BOURSE TO BE SET UP IN BOMBAY

The Federation of Indian Stock Exchanges (FISE) will promote a new bourse with a national reach, making it the third of its kind after the Bombay and the National bourses. The exchange, to be called the Indian Stock Exchanges Services Corporation (ISESC), will be formed by linking all 11 regional bourses. ISESC, which would be a company limited by guarantee, has approached the bourse regulator for the required approvals.
The Observer
MORGAN INVESTS 220 MLN RUPEES IN HCL-COMNET

Investment bankers J.P. Morgan announced an investment of 225 million rupees in HCL-Comnet, a business communications solutions company. J.P. Morgan agreed to buy a 20 percent share in HCL-Comnet at a premium of 80 rupees per 10 rupee share. The HCL-Comnet chairman said fresh shares would be issued for this purpose. The fresh equity would help finance a project which would enable clients to dial into the business communication infrastructure to be set up by HCL-Comnet.
